A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MedForge research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the appendix reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original detection experiments, automated reasoning-quality evaluations, and component, optimization, and backbone ablations in Tables 1–3.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds human evaluations, external-dataset experiments, failure analyses, and localization statistics in Appendix B.

M1.justification: The detector architecture, localize-then-analyze output, SFT-to-GSPO training, and coverage, formatting, and classification rewards are retained. Changing the appendix wording from 'IoU coverage' to 'Mask Coverage' aligns it with the existing Equation 7 rather than introducing a new objective.

E1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds evaluation on four external medical deepfake distributions: Med-Diffu, Synth-Pneumonia, Synth-Biomarker, and Med-Banana. This substantially extends evaluation beyond MedForge-90K and its internal cross-model and cross-forgery settings; the original modality and pathology coverage remains.

E2.justification: The original comparison lineups remain, and AIGC-Holmes is corrected to AIGI-Holmes, the same cited method. The added comparisons use narrower lineups: human evaluation omits SIDA-13B, while external OOD evaluation includes only FakeVLM, AIGI-Holmes, Qwen3-VL-Plus, and Gemini 3 Pro.

E3.justification: V2 introduces single-blind human ratings by two trained annotators on 100 cases and balances two fake-only external datasets with MIMIC-CXR real images at 1:1. It also revises the reported source-image count from 30,000 to 31,990. The original 50K/10K/30K experimental splits remain stated; rerunning those experiments is not established.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations and qualitative example, Appendix B adds human checks on automated judging, external-distribution robustness tests, failure breakdowns by pathology, modality, edit direction and lesion size, and localization diagnostics addressing possible oversized-box reward exploitation.

E5.justification: Table 9 newly reports localization dispersion and distribution summaries, including standard deviation, median, percentile, and threshold-exceedance rates. These describe variation across samples, not uncertainty across training runs. Repeated-run estimates, confidence intervals, and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their numerical results. New results include a third-ranked human average of 72.7%, external-dataset accuracies of 90.7–99.6%, and detailed failure and localization statistics. Table 5 also shows Gemini 3 Pro exceeding the proposed method on Med-Diffu F1, 90.1 versus 89.8.

T1.justification: The task formulation, optimization equations, coverage definition, and reward formulas are mathematically unchanged. The new localization discussion adds empirical interpretation and limitations, without a new formal result, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same benchmark, grounded pre-hoc detector, GSPO contributions, and principal performance claims. 'Expert-guided' becomes 'expert-aligned,' but the underlying account of guideline-based automated annotation remains the same.

C2.justification: Appendix B adds substantive interpretations of healthy-fundus false alarms, difficult MRI forgeries, coarse localization, and possible oversized-box solutions under the unchanged reward. It proposes size-aware regularization as future work. Section 5.2 also softens real-world applicability from a guarantee to a suggestion.

D1.justification: V2 adds per-editor counts and dataset identifiers in Table 10, identifies expert contributors, and advertises a named code/data repository plus model checkpoint instead of the anonymous code/data pointer. The appendix diagnoser becomes Gemini 3 Pro, consistent with the existing Figure 2. Core training hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting the external datasets and introductory discussion of medical AI and reasoning, and replaces the Stacchio inpainting citation with Rombach et al. The related-work argument and principal novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The retained text receives localized grammar, terminology, affiliation, and naming corrections. Funding and expert acknowledgements are added, and the original Appendices A/B become C/D after new acknowledgements and results sections. The main narrative is largely preserved.

P2.justification: V2 substantially expands the tabular presentation with Tables 4–10 covering human ratings, external evaluations, failure categories, localization distributions, and dataset inventory. The four existing figures and main tables retain their basic designs, with limited caption and layout refinements.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens validation of the central claims: v1 quantified explanation quality only through MLLM judges and evaluated generalization within MedForge-90K, whereas v2 adds human ratings and four external datasets. Failure and localization analyses also clarify important limitations. Reporting weaknesses temper these gains: the 95,276-image inventory is not reconciled with the retained 90,000-image splits, and Table 9 reports 20,000 true-positive forgeries despite 140 reported misses. The broader validation and more candid diagnostics nevertheless provide a substantial net improvement.
